improv_extras.concept: place particles on an aperiodic Penrose / quasicrystal tiling so the lattice never repeats yet stays ordered

v1.feedback: The Penrose P3 subdivision is mathematically correct and the dome-of-leaves reliquary form reads clearly within 2 seconds — bone and umber on near-black is a textbook restrained palette. Two things to refine: the leaf geometry is only 2 triangles per instance, so at distance it reads more as a faceted shell than a tiled canopy — adding a slight center ridge or curl to each kite would give the surface the organic depth a reliquary deserves. Second, the chain lineage from parent jgt (incantation) is invisible — consider keeping a trace of the parent's character (glyph fragments, calligraphic stroke paths woven into the tile edges) so the piece reads as incantation *transformed by* Penrose lattice rather than a fresh Penrose build.
